title: What a label must say
subtitle: The compulsory information
objectives: List the information most labels must show

steps.title: The essentials
steps.body: Most wine labels must show the producer or bottler, the country of origin, the alcohol by volume, the volume of the bottle and allergen warnings. Wines with a geographical indication must name it. Since December 2023, EU labels must also give nutrition and ingredient information, often through a QR code.

steps.title: Vintage and sulphites
steps.body: The vintage is the year the grapes were picked. In the EU, if it is stated, at least 85% of the grapes must be from that year. Wines with over 10 mg/l of sulphur dioxide must say contains sulphites. Almost all wines do, since sulphur dioxide protects against oxygen and bacteria, and yeast makes a little naturally.
steps.highlight: Vintage: at least 85% from that year in the EU

steps.prompt: What does the vintage on a European label mean?
options: The year the wine was bottled
The year at least 85% of the grapes were harvested
The year the vineyard was planted
The year the wine was released
steps.explanation: Vintage is the harvest year. In the EU, at least 85% of the grapes must come from the stated year.

steps.title: Allergens
steps.body: Wines fined with egg or milk products must say so if any residue remains. Many vegans look for wines fined with bentonite clay or pea protein instead, or unfined wines. Some producers now state vegan on the label, but that term isn't regulated everywhere.
steps.highlight: Egg and milk fining must be declared

steps.prompt: A wine labelled contains sulphites has had unusually large amounts of chemicals added.
steps.explanation: Not true. The warning applies above 10 mg/l, which covers almost every wine. Yeast produces some sulphur dioxide itself.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels must show producer, origin, abv, volume and allergens
In the EU, a stated vintage means at least 85% of grapes from that year
Contains sulphites applies to almost all wines
